segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: After Yusuf's brothers accused their father with the words: "Inna abana lafi dalalin mubin" – indeed, our father is in clear error.
Why? Because he loves Yusuf and his brother more than us. What happened, what was the solution, what was the solution to this problem of theirs?
They say: "Uqtulu Yusufa" – kill Yusuf. You see, dear brothers, how they agreed, it comes out: what is the solution? Kill Yusuf. "Or," they say, "take him away to some distant land,
where our father cannot see him, so that our father will turn to you and his love will be reserved for you alone.
وَتَكُونُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ قَوْمًا صَالِحِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “…and after that you will be a righteous people.” (Yusuf 12:9)

segmenti.tekst: And after that, after that deed, after that killing, you will be," they say, "righteous people." You will repent and you will be righteous people.
So, dear brothers, they had a problem. The problem was that their father loved Yusuf more, as they saw it. The solution was to kill him. And what was the outcome?

They say: our father will love us after that. How did they want to make up for it? All through repentance, by repenting. And we see, dear brothers, that many people today fall into the same trap that Yusuf's brothers fell into.

You have a man who is faced with the temptation of fornication, and he says: "I will do this now, and then, in sha Allah, I will repent." Or he gets the chance to take a lot of money through some deed, haram money,

and he says: "I will take this money now, and then I will repent." And so Yusuf's brothers fell into the same trap. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ" – and Shaytan made what they were doing seem fair to them. So whenever a person sets out to do something haram, Shaytan makes it look even more attractive to him, paints it for him, just as he painted for Yusuf's brothers that

treacherous plan of theirs, that treacherous plan of theirs. First: who will guarantee to that man that he will repent afterwards? Second: who will guarantee to him that he will live long enough to repent?

And third: who guarantees to him that Allah will forgive him that sin? And believe me, because of this kind of thinking on the part of certain people, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, may, for a small sin, distance a person miles away from Islam and from the faith.

He may distance him from the faith. That is why a person needs to be careful about things like this, very, very careful. After Yusuf's brothers had agreed [unclear], the heart of one of them, that is, one of these ten brothers, softened a little.
And one of them said: "Do not kill Yusuf, let us not go that far.
وَأَلْقُوهُ فِي غَيَابَتِ الْجُبِّ
segmenti.prevod: “…but throw him into the bottom of the well…” (Yusuf 12:10)

segmenti.tekst: I have," he says, "another solution: let us throw him into a well. Let us throw him into a well.
يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السَّيَّارَةِ

We will throw him," he says, "into a well where caravans pass by, so that some caravan will take him and carry him far away." Because what is our goal, after all? Our goal is to separate Yusuf from our father,
so that he no longer sees him. And in time he will forget him and turn to us. And he will love only us and care only for us.

Further, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala… So they came to their father once they had agreed, once they had agreed on that vile plan, and they said: "O our father" – and they speak to him tenderly – "O our dear daddy,
why," they say, "do you not trust us with Yusuf? Why are you not sure of our love for Yusuf?
For," they say, "we only wish him well. We only wish him well." You see, dear brothers, how they had already changed their tune and their behaviour towards Yusuf.
This also indicates that, after this vile plan of theirs, they tried several times to take Yusuf, to take him along with them, to herd the livestock and so on, and so forth,

in order to get rid of him. "Why are you not sure of our good intentions towards Yusuf?" They say: "Send him with us tomorrow," they say, "so that he can enjoy himself a little and play a little" – since Yusuf was younger – "and," they say, "we will look after him, we will look after him." You see, dear brothers, how, how rotten this plan of theirs was, how rotten this plan of theirs was,

that they would behave in this way towards their own, their own brother. And how much Shaytan influences a person. That is why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: "وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ" – do not follow – what? – the footsteps of Shaytan.

Because Shaytan will not approach a person and say to him: "Go and commit fornication all at once." Instead he says: "Take a look," then "look a little more closely," then "send a message," and so on. And all of those are, all of those are footsteps. Just as with his brothers: everything gradually, little by little, until they came to the point of killing Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam. As for Ya'qub's answer, in sha Allah, we will continue tomorrow,
in sha Allahu ta'ala. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to keep you in goodness, and, in sha Allah, we will see each other tomorrow. As-salamu alaykum.
